test: noiseless ORACLE bias, e8 (all graphs/designs/shapes run)
decision_rule: supported if max|bias|<1e-8 (machine precision); refuted if any |bias|>5 MC SE

test: noisy ORACLE_D bias in units of its MC SE, e1,e2,e3,e5
decision_rule: supported if share |z|>3 below 0.05 (expect ~0.003 under H0)

test: e9 noiseless OLS_f bias vs exact-binomial closed form (theory_bias.py)
statistic: max|dev|=0.041, median|dev|=0.0012, share |dev|<3 MC SE=1.000, corr=1.0000 over 144 cells
decision_rule: supported if corr>0.99 and median|dev|<0.01 (bias scale 0.1-5); report share within 3 MC SE
note: large-degree shortcut gamma*(h'(p)-1): median|dev|=0.088, max 3.312; deviations from the exact form exceed the MC SE in 0% of cells (finite-sample/clustering of assignments, not studied further)

test: e10 concave spillover: OLS_f bias vs n (SBM, 1k-20k, Bernoulli)
decision_rule: supported if |bias| at the largest n is >=70% of that at n=1000 for both p (sampling error would fall like n^-1/2, to ~22%)

statistic: median Spearman(|bias|,curvature) over graph x design = 0.92 (min 0.81, n=12); gamma is not varied in e9
decision_rule: supported if median rho>0.8; gamma-dependence is NOT tested here (e9 fixes gamma) - see note
note: gamma x curvature interaction: only the curvature factor is varied in e9; the gamma factor is covered by e2 (gamma fixed 2) and not separately by this test

test: e3 ER Bernoulli(0.5), OLS_f: log SD ~ log n + log d
decision_rule: supported if both exponents within 0.05 of prediction

test: e3 SBM + Louvain-cluster design, OLS_f: log SD ~ log n + log d
decision_rule: descriptive (the prediction is stated for Bernoulli designs)

test: e4 SD vs p, OLS_f, linear truth
statistic: ego-FB: slope of log SD on log sqrt(1/(p(1-p)))=0.59 (4 p-values); SBM: slope of log SD on log sqrt(1/(p(1-p)))=1.03 (4 p-values); Stanford3: slope of log SD on log sqrt(1/(p(1-p)))=0.96 (4 p-values)
decision_rule: supported if slope within [0.7,1.3] (pred 1) for every graph

test: e4 matched-resolution comparison of Louvain vs random clusters (OLS_f RMSE; DM |bias|)
statistic: Louvain RMSE<random in 72% of 36 matched OLS_f cells; DM |bias| smaller in 100%; ego-FB/concave: median RMSE louvain=0.48 vs random=1.27; |bias| 0.02 vs 0.16 | ego-FB/linear: median RMSE louvain=0.43 vs random=0.98; |bias| 0.01 vs 0.06 | SBM/concave: median RMSE louvain=0.37 vs random=0.74; |bias| 0.06 vs 0.47 | SBM/linear: median RMSE louvain=0.35 vs random=0.50; |bias| 0.01 vs 0.01 | Stanford3/concave: median RMSE louvain=0.62 vs random=0.37; |bias| 0.17 vs 0.14 | Stanford3/linear: median RMSE louvain=0.53 vs random=0.27; |bias| 0.03 vs 0.00
decision_rule: supported if good clusters have lower RMSE in >=75% of matched cells and random clusters show no gain over Bernoulli

test: e4 planted-block quality (within-block edge fraction 0.8/0.9/0.97), linear truth
decision_rule: descriptive: monotone improvement in RMSE with quality would support H5

test: e1 DM bias slope in gamma (truth: GATE = tau + gamma; DM sees tau only under Bernoulli)
statistic: Bernoulli(0.5): slope -1.000..-0.999 over 6 graphs; Louvain clusters: -0.79..-0.06
decision_rule: supported if Bernoulli slopes within 0.05 of -1 (proportional to gamma)

test: e1 DM wins RMSE at gamma=0, loses at larger gamma
statistic: DM wins at gamma=0 in 12/12 graph x design; first gamma at which OLS_f beats DM: BA/bern=0.5, BA/louv=0.5, ego-FB/bern=1, ego-FB/louv=4, ER/bern=0.5, ER/louv=0.5, SBM/bern=0.5, SBM/louv=2, Stanford3/bern=0.5, Stanford3/louv=2, WS/bern=1, WS/louv=1
decision_rule: supported if DM wins at gamma=0 in all combinations and OLS_f wins by gamma<=4

statistic: HajekFull n_rep median 282 (of ~400), n_nan median 118; HajekKappa n_rep median 400.0
decision_rule: reported as unestimable when n_rep<10 (full-neighbourhood exposure units absent at this degree)
note: no extra Hajek design run; the statement 'Hajek is biased if its exposure model is wrong' is therefore not tested

test: e6 mean 95% CI coverage by SE type (degenerate cell e6 BA acl0.5 excluded: one analysis cluster)
statistic: linear/ORACLE_D: hc=0.60, cl=0.86, hac1=0.76, hac2=0.91 | linear/OLS_f: hc=0.61, cl=0.88, hac1=0.76, hac2=0.91 | concave/ORACLE_D: hc=0.63, cl=0.87, hac1=0.78, hac2=0.91 | concave/OLS_f: hc=0.39, cl=0.69, hac1=0.54, hac2=0.70; n cells linear/OLS_f=28
decision_rule: supported if HC0 coverage <0.85 for correctly specified/linear cells and cluster-robust/HAC raise it; coverage loses under bias (concave OLS_f < 0.85)

test: e2 graph family: OLS_f RMSE (Bernoulli 0.5, linear truth)
statistic: SBM=0.47, BA=0.26, WS=0.51, ER=0.27, Stanford3=0.26, ego-FB=0.92 (n,d differ across graphs: confounded)
decision_rule: supported if both heavy-tailed graphs (BA, Stanford3) have RMSE above the median of the six graphs; refuted if both are below it

test: e7 two-hop interference fitted with 1-hop features (OLS_f) vs the 2-hop-aware ORACLE_D, Bernoulli 0.5
statistic: BA: OLS_f bias -1.02, rmse 1.05 vs ORACLE_D rmse 1.14, ego-FB: OLS_f bias -0.86, rmse 1.26 vs ORACLE_D rmse 1.93, ER: OLS_f bias -1.01, rmse 1.04 vs ORACLE_D rmse 1.22, SBM: OLS_f bias -0.92, rmse 1.04 vs ORACLE_D rmse 2.75, Stanford3: OLS_f bias -0.96, rmse 0.99 vs ORACLE_D rmse 1.85, WS: OLS_f bias -0.40, rmse 0.68 vs ORACLE_D rmse 1.03
decision_rule: supported if OLS_f |bias|>0.3 on all graphs
note: ORACLE_D here = [1, z, f1, f2, log-degree]: the correctly specified model (2-hop exposure + degree-dependent baseline). Its RMSE is variance-dominated and exceeds that of the misspecified OLS_f in most graphs (bias-variance trade-off); 'ORACLE' (no degree term) is not correctly specified in e7 because baselines depend on degree

test: e1 gamma=0, Bernoulli(0.5): SD of OLS_f over SD of DM (no interference, both unbiased)
decision_rule: supported if the ratio exceeds 3 on every graph

test: e2 OLS_f: bias vs variance by spillover shape (gamma=2, 6 graphs x 4 designs)
statistic: concave: median |bias|/GATE=0.14, bias-dominated (bias^2>RMSE^2/2) in 33% of 24 cells; convex: median |bias|/GATE=0.14, bias-dominated (bias^2>RMSE^2/2) in 38% of 24 cells; linear: median |bias|/GATE=0.01, bias-dominated (bias^2>RMSE^2/2) in 0% of 24 cells; sigmoid: median |bias|/GATE=0.34, bias-dominated (bias^2>RMSE^2/2) in 67% of 24 cells
decision_rule: bias dominates for sigmoid, not for linear (bias-dominated share 0 for linear)

test: e2 RMSE comparisons over 96 graph x shape x design cells
statistic: OLS_f<DM in 85%; ORACLE_D<OLS_f in 85%; OLS_quad<OLS_f in 14%; GBM<OLS_f in 18%
note: OLS_quad and GBM rarely beat OLS_f: extra flexibility costs variance at these n and often extrapolates badly
